cases.answer: Two strengths I bring are patience and organisation. Last winter I covered the phone queue on a Saturday when a courier partner's tracking system went down and about forty customers were waiting on parcels due that day. I was the shift lead on the floor, so deciding who to call back and in what order was mine to own. I pulled the list of affected orders, phoned the oldest ones first and booked redelivery slots with the depot while my teammate sent text updates. By closing time we had reached 38 of the 40, and complaints on that batch dropped to two.

cases.answer: A strength of mine is staying steady when people are angry. At my shop till a man told me, "You people never listen, I want my money back now," and put his receipt down hard on the counter. I was the only person on the desk, so it was my call. I let him finish, repeated back what he had said, checked the receipt against the till and refunded the 24 pounds. He left saying it was fair enough and came back the next week. I learned to let people finish before I answer.

When I finish a call I run the same checks every time. First I read back what the customer asked and what I agreed, then I check that the notes I typed in the CRM match what was said, and finally I look at whether I gave any time promises I can really keep. This matters because a customer who repeats the same story to the next agent loses trust fast and our handle time goes up. Afterwards I tag any gaps, message the customer if I missed something, and add a line to our team wiki when I spot a repeated slip.
